item.title: Sánchez settles the debate: 2030 World Cup final will be held in Spain
item.description: Sánchez settles the debate: 2030 World Cup final will be held in Spain Speaking to Mundo Deportivo, the prime minister champions Spain’s stadiums as hosts for the decisive match and takes a political swipe following the controversy over the Barça star’s shirt. The debate over the venue for the biggest match on the planet now has an official answer. In an interview with Mundo Deportivo , Pedro Sánchez was unequivocal about the allocation of venues for the global tournament jointly hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco : the 2030 World Cup final will be played on Spanish soil. "We have some of the best stadiums in the world, extraordinary fans and a country that knows what it means to make history through sport," the prime minister said, dispelling doubts about Spain’s bid in the face of Morocco’s ambitions. Beyond the footballing spectacle, Sánchez stressed that the tournament must leave a lasting legacy through jobs and new grassroots sports facilities, giving young people somewhere to start emulating their idols. The swipe over Lamine Yamal’s shirt The prime minister did not shy away from the social and political dimensions surrounding Spain’s national team, highlighting Lamine Yamal’s status as a role model for younger generations and dreaming of lifting "our third World Cup in front of our own fans". However, the most viral headline came when he addressed Xavier García Albiol’s recent comments about the Barça winger: "Unlike Albiol, I would wear Lamine’s shirt, or that of any player on Spain’s national team. Whoever they vote for, whatever they think or whoever they pray to". A staunch defence of diversity in the La Roja dressing room that once again puts football at the heart of the national conversation. item.title: What time is Rutgers football vs. Michigan State? TV, prediction
item.description: PISCATAWAY – Rutgers football hasn’t enjoyed much momentum this season, but the Scarlet Knights are riding some heading into their season finale. Coming off a wild 25-24 road win at Penn State, the program’s first win over the Nittany Lions in 38 years, Rutgers will host Michigan State Saturday at SHI Stadium in Week 13 of the college football season. With a win, the Scarlet Knights would finish the 2026 campaign 4-8. Quarterback AJ Surace, playing with three broken ribs, is coming off his best game so far, going 24-of-39 for 178 yards with one touchdown at Penn State. Michigan State has struggled badly in Pat Fitzgerald’s first year at the helm, and like Rutgers is 3-8 overall but has fared worse in Big Ten play, going just 1-7. It’s been ugly in East Lansing. Which team will avoid a three-win season? Here’s how to watch and find out: Rutgers football schedule: Scarlet Knights' next game Rutgers plays Michigan State on Saturday, Nov. 28 at SHI Stadium in Piscataway, N.J. in a Week 13 game. What time is Rutgers vs. Michigan State? Kickoff is scheduled for 4:15 p.m. ET. What channel is Rutgers vs. Michigan State? The game will be televised on Big Ten Network. Watch Rutgers vs. Michigan State live on Fubo (free trial for new subscribers) Rutgers vs. Michigan State spread Rutgers is a 3.5-point underdog, according to Vegas Insider. Rutgers vs. Michigan State prediction Much like Rutgers at this point, Michigan State has absolutely nothing to play for except for pride. But I like Greg Schiano getting his team prepared for that spot more than Pat Fitzgerald. The Scarlet Knights fought for Schiano at Penn State, and he'll have them ready against Michigan State. Rutgers has also seemed to have the Spartans ' number in recent years, having won three of the last five meetings. Scarlet Knights QB AJ Surace is coming off his best game yet. I'll take the Scarlet Knights getting past MSU. Score prediction: Rutgers 27, Michigan State 24 Rutgers vs. Michigan State tickets Buy tickets for Rutgers vs. Michigan State on StubHub. item.title: Real Madrid fringe star finally sees things falling into place at club and international level
item.description: Real Madrid fringe star finally sees things falling into place at club and international level Brahim Diaz could be approaching an important turning point in his Real Madrid career, with a contract extension, Endrick’s injury and a potentially historic decision involving Morocco all offering reasons for optimism. According to AS , the Spanish-Moroccan forward is expected to benefit from greater opportunities under Jose Mourinho following Endrick’s recent injury, while his renewal with Real Madrid is already agreed in principle. The midfielder’s challenge is now to turn his limited playing time into a more regular role, starting with the Champions League meeting against PSV . Endrick’s injury gives Brahim Diaz an opportunity at Real Madrid It is to be noted that Brahim has played just 248 minutes this season, making him the 18th-most-used player in the Real Madrid squad. To put it in perspective, only Endrick, Eder Militão, Andriy Lunin, Carlos Espi and Thiago Pitarch have featured for fewer minutes. However, Endrick’s absence for approximately three weeks could create an opportunity for Brahim to challenge for more playing time on the right flank, where Arda Guler has recently been preferred. The Moroccan international has already demonstrated his effectiveness in the Champions League, having registered three assists in just 100 minutes, making him Real Madrid’s leading assist provider in the competition. Endrick’s injury has opened doors for Brahim Diaz. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) The upcoming meeting with PSV therefore offers another opportunity to strengthen his case for greater involvement. Real Madrid prepare Brahim’s contract extension Another important development concerns Brahim’s contractual future. His current agreement expires on June 30, 2027, but Real Madrid have already reached an agreement to extend his stay until 2031 , with an announcement expected soon. For what it is worth, Brahim has consistently prioritised remaining at the Santiago Bernabeu despite receiving limited opportunities. His renewal would reinforce Real Madrid’s confidence in his long-term contribution, although a new contract does not automatically guarantee a more prominent position in Mourinho’s plans. There could be more good news for Brahim Away from club football, Brahim is approaching another potentially significant moment in his career. Brahim Diaz could be in line for two international recognitions in the coming weeks. (Photo by Molly Darlington/Getty Images) This is because the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) is scheduled to announce its decision on November 24, regarding Senegal’s appeal against the decision to award Morocco the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title. Senegal originally won the final 1-0 after extra time. However, CAF subsequently overturned the result and awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory after Senegal’s players temporarily left the pitch in protest following a controversial penalty decision. item.title: Enmarket Arena to host Savannah Shootout high school hoops event
item.description: After a year off, the Savannah Shootout is returning to Enmarket Area as a showcase of Coastal Empire high school basketball talent. The event, now in its third year, will be held at Enmarket Arena on Friday and Saturday, Nov. 27 and 28. The Savannah High boys team, which won a state title in 2025, is among the teams set to compete. On the boys side, Savannah High, Johnson, Groves, Calvary Day, Windsor Forest, Bradwell Institute and Long County are among the teams set to compete. On the girls side, Jenkins and South Effingham and Tattnall County, which is also sending its boys team, are among the teams in the mix. "We won a state title two years ago and we're hoping to live up to those expectations and win it again this season," Savannah High coach George Brown said. "Our goal is always going to be State Championship or bust. I think we have the team to do it this year. Our team is different this year, we're playing together and not being as selfish as we were last year." The Blue Jackets are led by Martaiveis Rice, a senior who averaged 18.6 points and 8.4 rebounds per game last season, and junior Renard Jackson (17.5 ppg, 6.2 rpg), who were both All-Greater Savannah first-team selections last season when the Blue Jackets reached the second round of the state tourney. "Playing in the Shootout is a beautiful tradition and it's been impactful for our program," Brown said. "It gives you a playoff atmosphere early in the season." Bradwell Institute is playing in the event for the first time as the Tigers will face Long County Saturday at 6:30 p.m. Bradwell has a big-time senior guard leading the way in Zi'on Thomas, an All-Greater Savannah first-team pick last year when he averaged 15.5 points per game. There will be a strong local matchup on Friday when Windsor Forest faces off with Groves, which is led by Kavalee Godboldte and point guard Kyleiq MacKey. Windsor Forest features Kayleb Garner. "This event is big for the city of Savannah," Groves coach Kevin Evans said. "It's getting bigger every year and does a lot for the exposure of our teams and players." On Saturday, the Calvary Day boys face Johnson in a local matchup, with Savannah High and Groves closing things out with the Shootout's final game. Calvary Day has a new coach in Josh Dannenfelser, who will be matching wits with veteran Johnson coach Chuck Campbell. The Jenkins girls reached the Class 3A Elite Eight last year, a season after losing on a buzzer-beater in the Final Four. Brianna Brooker's squad features returning standouts in seniors I'Yarna Lee and Angelique Fleming and junior Jayla Johnson. "There is so much talent from our area playing in the Shootout on both the boys and girls sides," Brooker said. "It's an amazing opportunity for us to showcase our talent." The South Effingham girls are another team to watch at the event. Alexus Parker's squad is off to a 2-0 start after impressive wins over Jenkins and Richmond Hill. item.title: 'He’s won everything' - Jose Mourinho explains Vini Jr's recent Real Madrid struggles
item.description: Real Madrid v RC Celta de Vigo - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Jose Mourinho has fiercely backed Vinicius Junior to return to his full potential ahead of Real Madrid's Champions League meeting with PSV. The Los Blancos boss insists the Brazilian's recent dip in momentum was merely caused by a four-match suspension rather than a lack of motivation. Mourinho backs Vinicius Junior ahead of PSV Mourinho has backed Vinicius to return to his peak level ahead of Madrid's Champions League clash with PSV . Speaking at his pre-match press conference at the Santiago Bernabeu, the Portuguese coach defended the Brazilian forward before Matchday 5 of the European campaign. This season, Vinicius has recorded only one goal and three assists in 13 appearances across all competitions. Despite recent scrutiny surrounding the winger's form, Mourinho insists age and hunger are firmly on his player's side. Youth and empathy key to Brazilian's revival Mourinho believes observers often overlook just how young Vinicius remains because of his rapid rise to superstardom. Unlike veteran players who naturally battle physical decline, the Madrid boss stressed that the forward retains all the attributes required to thrive. "He’ll return to his full potential," Mourinho said on the club's official website . "He’s young, and sometimes when players approach or pass the age of 30, they struggle to maintain their ideal physical condition and some lose a bit of their motivation. Vini Jr. is young, and people can forget that he arrived very young and reached an extremely high level far too soon. "He’s won everything, but when people were out to get him, he always said he’s a really good lad and very empathetic towards everyone. That’s a fundamental foundation." Suspension disrupted forward's momentum and confidence Mourinho explained that Vinicius' recent stop-start rhythm stemmed directly from a disciplinary setback rather than any deeper issue. According to the manager, a four-match ban halted his progress right after he had demonstrated his match-winning quality against Villarreal . "He had a very positive impact the other day and I remember that against Villarreal he turned the game around, but he was out for four matches due to his sending-off and that disrupted his development and his confidence," the manager noted. "At the weekend he came on well and helped turn the match around." Madrid prepare for Champions League test With his confidence boosted by an impactful weekend appearance and full backing from his manager, Vinicius will look to carry that momentum onto the European stage. Madrid welcome PSV to the Santiago Bernabeu knowing a strong display from their dynamic winger could prove decisive on Matchday 5. Mourinho will hope the Brazilian translates his recent cameo into a commanding performance under the Champions League lights. For Vinicius Junior, the visit of PSV offers an immediate opportunity to validate his manager's faith and reignite his campaign.

item.title: Future Hillsdale teammates carry Whiteford, Ithaca into state finals
item.description: OTTAWA LAKE – Whiteford running back Brek Ruddy and Ithaca quarterback Gibson Rondy will be teammates next season at Hillsdale College. Someone is going to have bragging rights when they arrive on campus. Their teams will meet at Ford Field in Detroit for the Division 7 state football championship at 9:30 a.m. on Saturday, Nov. 28. They have been two of the most prolific offensive players in the state this season. Prep Football: Whiteford rolls to spot in state finals, Jefferson falls in semis Rondy has thrown for 2,570 yards and 32 touchdowns, but was more effective on the ground during the Yellowjackets’ 34-26 victory over defending state champion Menominee in the semifinals Saturday. He ran for 180 yards and 3 touchdowns. “He’s a big kid and a really good athlete,” Whiteford coach Todd Thieken said. “He can throw the ball all over the field and has a very strong arm. Lately his running game has been very dangerous.” Ruddy is closing in on the Monroe County Region record for rushing yards in a season with 2,379 yards through 13 games. That’s the second-highest total in Region history behind the 2,501 posted by Milan’s Ron Spears in 2007. “Number 22 at running back is an outstanding player,” Ithaca coach Jordan Hessbrook said. Ruddy has been unstoppable in the playoffs, running for 846 yards (211.5 per game) and 12 touchdowns in 4 games. “He’s special, but he doesn’t do all the things he does without the parts around him,” Thieken said. “The kids have done a great job of executing our offense the way it is set up.” The remarkable thing about Ruddy’s season is that none of the Bobcats’ starters on the offensive line were in those positions last season. Caden Stewart started a year ago, but at tight end. He shifted to tackle after the first game this season. Tackle Austin Billau, guards Jacoby Miller and Logan Sanjur, center Jackson Cousino and tight end Mason Luzier all were backups in 2025. Stewart and Billau are the only seniors on the line this season. Miller, Luzier and Cousino are juniors and Sanjur is a sophomore. “They have done a great job,” Thieken said. “All six kids have grown. It’s a testament to them and our offensive line coaches.” Assistant coaches Ben Avis, Bob Odrovick, Drew Knaggs and Lucas Teznar work the linemen. Knaggs (2022) and Tesznar (2017) both played for state championship teams at Whiteford. The Bobcats will need to overcome one of its biggest challenges of the season if they hope to put a third football state title in their trophy case. “They have won (five) state championships back in the day,” Thieken said. “They definitely know what it’s like to be at Ford Field. They have one of the best small, pubic-school football programs in the state.” Ford Field won’t be a mystery for Whiteford, either. Eight of the team’s 11 seniors were on the roster when the Bobcats lost in the Division 8 final in 2023. item.title: Texas Tech basketball heads to Vegas for Players Era 16 | Schedule, what to know
item.description: The Texas Tech basketball team is spending the week out in Las Vegas to take part in this year's version of the biggest non-conference tournament in the country, taking up a spot in the Players Era 16. The Red Raiders (5-0) have ample opportunity to improve their stock even more, starting with their opening game against Louisville. Other marquee names involved include Tennessee, St. John's and Alabama . Here's everything you need to know about the Players Era 16 and Texas Tech's involvement in the event. Texas Tech basketball's schedule for Players Era 16 The Red Raiders open play today (Nov. 24) at 7 p.m. Central against Louisville. Everybody is off on Wednesday and return to the court on Thursday when Tech will play either St. John's or Oregon. If Tech beats Louisville, they'll play at 8 p.m. Central on Thursday. If it loses, their second game will be 10:30 p.m. Central. Tech will then play one of Iowa State, San Diego State, Maryland or Tennessee on Friday. Possible game times for those contests are noon, 2 p.m., 8 p.m. or 10:30 p.m. Should Texas Tech get the fourth game for the championship, that will be played Saturday at 9:30 p.m. How the Players Era 16 works Last year's version of the event was an unmitigated mess that involved point differential and uneven scheduling to determine one true king. Things are much more laid out this time around. Two separate brackets featuring eight teams apiece will be played at the same time, Texas Tech's games being played at Michelob Ultra Arena. The other bracket will play its games inside T-Mobile Arena. Texas Tech takes on Louisville to open the event. Other teams in Tech's bracket include St. John's, Oregon, San Diego State, Iowa State, Maryland and Tennessee. In the other bracket, Kansas State, Gonzaga, Alabama, Baylor , Michigan, Creighton , TCU and Miami will be vying for the crown. Every team involved this week will get three guaranteed games, both brackets playing out entirely through seventh-place games. Teams that go 3-0 in their respective brackets will play a fourth game on Saturday against one another to determine the true Players Era 16 champion. As noted before the season , college teams are able to have up to 32 regular-season games on their schedule. Texas Tech has 32 accounted for, but that's assuming the Red Raiders were to get four games in Las Vegas. Shy of that, the Red Raiders will wind up with 31 total regular season games due to the uncertain nature of the fourth game coming to fruition this weekend. The Big 12 and Players Era also have a direct connection as the top eight teams in the conference standings each year will earn automatic bids into the event each year through 2030. BYU and Arizona would've been part of this year's field but had prior commitments to the Maui Invitational. Who will play for Texas Tech basketball? item.title: Meet the Gazette's All-Area Volleyball team
item.description: CHILLICOTHE — This past fall, the area was blessed with yet another outstanding volleyball season. Individual milestones, historic victories and lengthy tournament runs were all a part of the fun. Three area teams — Adena, Zane Trace and Southeastern — claimed district titles, while others took the next steps towards the future. Meet the Gazette's All-Area Volleyball team, a cast that helped their teams reach new heights. Offensive Player of the Year: Evelyn Hamman, Chillicothe, senior Hamman ends her career at Chillicothe with multiple program records under her belt. She finished the year with an area-leading 579 kills and led the Cavaliers to a district semifinal. OH: Calli Knight, Waverly, sophomore With a team-high 313 kills, Knight continued to transform into a formidable offensive threat. She also added 55 aces and 320 digs while helping her Tigers win 16 matches. Her future is bright. OH: Karlee Snavely, Zane Trace, junior Behind Snavely, ZT won its first district title since 2023. The junior was sensational, posting 496 kills — including the 1,000th of her career — and adding 52 aces, 47 blocks and 240 digs. OH: Brailee Hauswirth, Huntington, junior While proving her worth in all six rotations, Hauswirth came into her own as a junior. She led the team with 351 kills and a .276 hitting percentage. She also posted 46 aces and 280 digs. OH: Jill Butcher, Westfall, senior The Mustangs flew under the radar into a district final appearance this past fall. Butcher was the pilot. She ended the season with team-highs of 267 kills and 47 aces, alongside 228 digs. MH: Kylee Dunn, Southeastern, junior Dunn was an absolute menace all season, totaling a team-high 438 kills and 45 blocks. She also added 48 aces and 101 digs for good measure while collecting her 1,000th career kill. MH: Jacey Jones, Adena, junior Entering her senior year, Jones will have a total of 765 kills. 505 of those happened this fall as she led her Warriors to 16 victories and a regional final appearance. She’s flat-out special. MH: Charlotte Dennis, Unioto, junior The Shermans won their first SVC championship since 2023, and followed Dennis’ lead to get there. The junior put down a team-high 308 kills and added 73 blocks to her season totals. MH: Ryanne Moore, Piketon, senior When Moore was on the floor, Piketon was a dangerous team. The hard-hitting senior gave the ‘Streaks flashes of life, collecting 358 kills en route to her 1,000th career alongside 77 blocks. Fan-Favorite Player of the Year: Kinzli Batson, Unioto, junior The SVC’s Player of the Year was extraordinary all season, passing out 785 assists while tacking on 200 digs, 58 kills and 43 aces. She enters her senior year with 1,687 career assists. S: Isabella Witte, Chillicothe, senior No other area setter had as many assists as Witte, who tallied 808 this fall. item.title: Ducks' defensive effort done in by third-period mistakes in Seattle
item.description: Nov 23, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Anaheim Ducks center Mikael Granlund (64) and Seattle Kraken defenseman Josh Mahura (28) and Seattle Kraken defenseman Ryan Lindgren (55) plays the puck during the first period at Climate Pledge Arena. SEATTLE – The Anaheim Ducks finally strung together back-to-back solid overall defensive performances, but once again, it was the small moments in crucial areas that undid any steps forward. The Seattle Kraken scored the go-ahead goal three separate times in the third period–each on an Anaheim miscue–to overcome the Ducks, 3-2, on Monday at Climate Pledge Arena. Despite allowing only 33 shots over the last two games–a new franchise-best–Anaheim (11-13-1, 23 points) finished the four-game road trip winless (0-4-0) and has lost six of its last seven games following a five-game winning streak. "Terrible loss. Tough loss,” Joel Quenneville told local media in Seattle. “Thought we played two good games in a row, and should've got points in both of them and come up empty on a tough trip. Gotta go home and turn it around this week. We've got big games." Ducks played their first game without Leo Carlsson this season, as the No. 1 center is listed as day-to-day with an upper-body injury suffered on Saturday in Utah. Carlsson, who collided face first with the forearm of a linesman early in the second period of that game , did not skate at Ducks practice on Sunday in Seattle or their optional gameday morning skate on Monday. Beckett Sennecke missed his second game on injured reserve with an upper-body injury. Cutter Gauthier got the Ducks on the board off a Roger McQueen face-off win in the third period to even up the game, 1-1. Gauthier snapped a two-game goal drought following a prolific 10-game goal streak with his 18th goal of November. The 22-year-old is two goals shy of the NHL record for goals in a month of 20, which was last reached by Teemu Selanne in March 1993. Sam Colangelo scored his second goal of the season by putting home the rebound of a Frank Vatrano shot later in the third period to equalize again, 2-2. However, Seattle pushed ahead three times in the final frame–all on Ducks mistakes. Just under three minutes into the period, Ian Moore’s pass below the goal line was picked off by Matthew Wood and immediately sent to Ben Meyers crashing the slot for a one-timer, 1-0. Seven minutes later, a Vince Dunn point blast went through Lukáš Dostál, despite a clear view up the middle, for the 2-1 advantage. Finally, with under three minutes remaining, Nico Myatovic turned the puck over just outside the Anaheim blue line as Ian Moore went off for a change upon clearing the zone. The change with Tristan Luneau was slow, and as Seattle quickly turned up ice, Kaapo Kakko was sprung into the vacated space for a one-on-one dance around Dostál and the game-winner, 3-2. item.title: Stephen A. Smith calls out Draymond Green for going ‘too far’ with criticism of NBA veteran
item.description: Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images Things are never far from falling out when Stephen A. Smith and Draymond Green are involved, and a recent controversy includes an NBA veteran. The vibes in Golden State took a hit recently as the reality of playing without Steph Curry set in, but the Warriors are bouncing back of late with some surprise wins. As always, Draymond Green talks when he has something to back it up, so he’s responding to criticisms of his game this season. One of his responses to NBA veteran Eddie Johnson has rubbed up Stephen A. Smith the wrong way. Stephen A. Smith calls out Draymond Green Green was recently involved in a back-and-forth with Eddie Johnson, who is an NBA veteran and a current broadcaster for the Phoenix Suns. Johnson blamed Green for being mentally checked out after Curry’s injury, bringing up his lack of shot attempts this season to prove his point. Green’s shot attempts this season are down drastically, but when he’s locked in, he’s still one of the league’s best defenders. Green didn’t take kindly to being called out by Johnson, and hit back with a brutal riposte, calling Johnson a “loser” who just debates because he never won what Green has. Stephen A. Smith didn’t take kindly to it, and while he gave him a pass for responding to Johnson, he wasn’t so kind to Green calling Johnson a nobody. Speaking on the Stephen A. Smith show , he said: “I think that last part was going a bit too far. Eddie Johnson could ball, and Eddie Johnson was a damn good NBA player. We also know that he has a reputable basketball mind, a highly reputable basketball mind. “And the thing that I find a bit ironic is that you hear stuff like that from time to time about players when they’re commenting about former players, like, if you didn’t play at that level, you don’t really have any business talking about it. Well, Eddie Johnson did play at that level. So, is it really about what level you’re at, or is it more about the fact that somebody disagrees with you?” Green has never been one to listen to criticism constructively, and he’s built a career out of having a chip on his shoulder at all times. It leads to debates like these where he rubs people up the wrong way, which is what has happened with Johnson this time. With Green, it’s more about disagreeing with him rather than what level the criticism is coming from, and that has always been true, regardless of what he says. item.title: America 250: High school volleyball Mount Rushmore by position in Holland area
item.description: While we are still in America's 250th year, I am still in the historic mindset. I have read about 15 books on the American Revolution this year and as you saw during the summer, we did some 250 and Mount Rushmore lists for schools. One of the best parts about sports is being able to debate lists of the greatest athletes of all time. The Holland area has had great tradition in high school volleyball over the years. I am going to put together my Mt. Rushmore of high school volleyball position by position. Remember this is my opinion. If you disagree, feel free to let me know, but please do so in a civil manner. Civil debates about sports are really fun. So here we go with the Holland area high school volleyball Mt. Rushmore lists: OUTSIDE HITTER Sophie Riemersma, Zeeland East The Miss Volleyball finalist holds the area record for kills in a match (39), kills in a season (819) and kills in a career (2,271). She was all-state three times and went on to play and start at the NCAA Division I level at Miami (Ohio) and then Jacksonville State. Raegan Lantz, West Ottawa This tall outside hitter was all-state multiple times and reached 1,000 career kills. She went on to play and start at Miami (Ohio) at the NCAA Division I level. Cortney Lokker, West Ottawa This all-state athlete ushered in the superstar volleyball era in the Holland area. The all-state player went on to help GVSU win the NCAA championship. Kristen Etterbeek, Holland Christian This multi-sport star was a Miss Volleyball Finalist and as good at digging as she was at killing the ball. She led the Maroons to the state championship before going to play at Penn in the Ivy League. Debate: Hamilton's Jordan Pikaart was a sensational player who was all-state and would be the next on my list. Etterbeek and Pikaart were pretty even but Etterbeek got the nod since she led her team to a state championship. There are so many great outside hitters from the area: Aerin Baker, Ana Capotosto, Natalie Dunn, Katie Rietberg, Hannah Petroelje, Jamie Kraker, Corbyn Wayner, current Zeeland East senior Lizzie Risdon and more. MIDDLE HITTER Alyssa Garvelink, Holland Christian The top player in area history, Garvelink was a three-time all-state performer and Miss Volleyball Finalist as a senior. She went on to become an All-American at Michigan State and still plays professionally for the Grand Rapids Rise. Mackenzie Stephens, West Ottawa This middle hitter was a Miss Volleyball Finalist and two-time all-state performer with a strong swing and elite block. item.title: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟
item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. In his first full campaign, the Man City-bound starlet emerged as one of the league's most exciting young talents, finishing with with a career-high 23 goal contributions (nine goals, 14 assists) in 29 appearances, and recorded a goal contribution in 10 consecutive matches, the longest such run by a teenager in MLS history. Both his total of 23 goal contributions and his 14 assists are the most ever by a teenager in a single MLS season. Sullivan's form also earned him MLS Player of the Month honors for September 2026. At 17 years and two days old, he became the youngest winner of the award in league history. His production on the club level soon translated to the international stage. Sullivan received his first call-up to the US men's national team in September and made his debut against Peru, becoming the second-youngest player in USMNT history to start a match. He has since collected four senior caps and added another milestone to his résumé by scoring against Mexico at 17 years and five days old, making him the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history.

item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn’t. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. One of the biggest problems that NYCFC faced this season – especially during its struggles in the second half – had been allowing late goals that would cost the club points, or matches altogether. And the club dealt with a number of injuries during the course of the season, while also playing much of the year without one of its top scorers, Alonso Martinez, as he recovered from a torn ACL he suffered last fall. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
